result.text: E-2194 means the Ashby tumble dryer’s factory reset was interrupted before its saved settings could be cleared, so your previous preferences may still be active.
KX-9283 is the Wi-Fi module for the Ashby tumble dryer. It connects the dryer to the Halvard Home app.
Error E-7084 means the Vale fridge freezer’s vibration sensor has detected excessive movement while the compressor is running. An uneven position or contact with nearby furniture may be the cause.
KX-3107 is the voice pairing module for the Orrin heat pump.
Error E-6076 means water has remained in the dishwasher’s base for more than three minutes after draining started. A blocked filter or kinked drain hose is the usual cause.
None of the passages identifies part KX-3673.
E-6292 means the Fenwick cooker hood has an electrical insulation fault in its fan motor. Stop using it, switch off its power, and have a qualified electrician assess it.
The passages do not identify part KX-6507. P1 lists KX-6505 as the Lumen thermostat’s replacement mounting backplate.

E-5107 means mains power was interrupted while the compressor was running. The heat pump pauses to protect the compressor during restart. When power returns, leave it connected for five minutes, then press the controller’s power button once and select your usual heating setting.
KX-3926 is the washable metal grease filter for the Fenwick cooker hood.
None of the passages explains error E-3865.
The passages don’t identify part KX-3452.
The passages do not explain error E-3873.
KX-7011 is the sealing strip fitted beneath the Corra induction hob’s glass edge. It must lie flat all the way around before the hob is lowered into place.

E-4805 means the Tessa dishwasher’s digital warranty record is missing its purchase date, so the warranty can’t be confirmed automatically. It doesn’t mean the warranty has expired. Find your proof of purchase and contact Halvard Home support with the purchase date and serial number.
KX-1639 is the supplied charging dock for the Mira robot vacuum.
E-6736 means the Brio kettle’s lid locking clip is not holding the lid securely shut.
KX-9495 is the heating relay module for the Lumen smart thermostat.
E-3293 means the Corra induction hob’s moisture sensor detected condensation beneath the control panel and stopped heating as a precaution.
KX-8033 isn’t identified in any of the passages.
E-7160 means the Orrin heat pump’s warranty record is missing its installation date, so the system can’t verify the remaining warranty period. It’s a registration issue, not a heating fault.
KX-9996 is the voice connection module in an Ashby tumble dryer. It connects the dryer to a voice assistant.
E-1216 means the Halvard Home Fenwick cooker hood’s control board cannot detect the fan motor’s speed, so it stops the fan.
The passages don’t identify part KX-5912.
Error E-4021 on a Halvard Home Tessa dishwasher means the water has not drained within three minutes. A blocked drain filter is the most common cause.
KX-2446 is the drain pump fitted to the Halvard Home Keel washing machine.
E-3946 means the Corra induction hob’s lid sensor detects that the protective lid isn’t fully closed. The lid may be obstructed or its hinge may be misaligned.
KX-5646 is the replacement cooling fan for a Corra induction hob.
The passages don’t identify error E-6779. Check the appliance’s manual or contact Halvard Home support for its meaning.
KX-7896 is the Lumen thermostat’s room temperature sensor module. It provides temperature readings for automatic heating control.
The passages do not mention error E-9454. They describe E-9544 as an overheating temperature-sensor warning during Eco mode.
KX-8645 is the removable filter for the Tessa dishwasher.
The passages do not mention error E-8255. They describe Mira error E-8250, which means the battery is too cold to charge safely.
KX-3056 is the Brio kettle’s wireless pairing module. It connects the kettle to the Halvard Home app so you can link a supported voice assistant.
The passages don’t identify error E-5328, so its meaning can’t be determined from the information provided. Contact Halvard Home support and give them the error code and your appliance model.
The passages don’t identify part KX-8618. They list KX-1618 as the replacement drying rack for an Ashby tumble dryer.
E-9509 means the delay-start timer has lost its saved countdown, so the dishwasher pauses instead of starting unexpectedly.
The passages do not identify part KX-1377.
The passages don’t mention error E-9215, so its meaning can’t be determined from the information provided.
KX-1060 is the power recovery control module for a Corra induction hob.
Your Brio kettle supports **2.4 GHz Wi‑Fi**. If your router has separate 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz networks, connect it to the 2.4 GHz one.

Before leaving, run a wash to clear any dirty dishes. When it finishes, unload the dishwasher, let the interior cool, clean the filter according to the user manual, and wipe the door seals with a soft, damp cloth.

If the cottage will be empty for an extended period, switch off the electricity and close the dishwasher’s water supply valve. Leave the door slightly open if it is safe to do so. If the cottage could freeze, ask a qualified installer whether the appliance should be drained. On your return, restore both supplies and check for leaks before running a wash.

Leave a short, clear instruction note beside each laundry appliance:

- **Tumble dryer:** Clean the lint filter after every load; check care labels; don’t overload it; keep the area around it clear; and stay in the property until the full programme, including cooling, has finished.
- **Washing machine:** Check hoses for leaks or damage, turn on the water supply before washing, choose a programme suited to the care labels, and measure detergent for the load and water hardness. Before leaving, remove laundry, check the drum, wipe the door seal, switch off the machine and water supply, and leave the door slightly open if safe.

The warranty information conflicts: one passage says **two years from purchase**, while another says **66 months from delivery**. The 66-month cover starts on the delivery date, not the purchase or installation date. Contact Halvard Home with your purchase and delivery records to confirm which terms apply.

Stop cooking and switch the hob off using its controls. Check that the control panel is clear and dry, and let hot surfaces cool before wiping them. Follow the instructions for the specific error if you know its code—for example, some moisture warnings require leaving the hob off for a set time before restoring power.

If the warning returns, leave the hob switched off and contact Halvard Home support. Note what flashes or appears on the display and when it happens. Don’t remove the glass or attempt internal repairs.

Stop the programme, switch off and unplug the dryer, and let it cool. Clean and securely refit the lint filter, empty and refit the water tank if your model has one, and check that clothing isn’t caught in the door. Reconnect it and try the programme again.

If a fault code appears, note exactly what it says; you can also check that accessible air vents are clear. If the warning or code returns, stop using the dryer and contact Halvard Home support with the light or code and your model details. Don’t remove panels or attempt internal repairs. If you notice smoke or a burning smell, do not restart it.

Ice or frost inside the dishwasher isn’t normal. Don’t start a programme. Switch the dishwasher off and contact Halvard Home support for advice before using it again. Don’t use boiling water or sharp tools to remove the ice.

Stop the dryer immediately. Switch it off and unplug it if it’s safe, and don’t run another cycle to test it. If there’s smoke or flame, keep the door closed, leave the property and call 999—don’t use water or move the appliance. If there’s no sign of fire, leave it unplugged until completely cool; then you can clear fluff from the lint filter and check that external vents are unobstructed. Don’t use it again until a qualified appliance technician has checked it.

Set a scheduled start for the time you want the heating to begin—not for the number of minutes to wait. For example, if it’s 18:00 and you want a one-hour delay, set the start time to 19:00. Choose your target temperature, save the schedule, and check that it’s enabled for the right day. Heating will start only if the room is cooler than your target.

To safely relocate your Ashby tumble dryer:

1. Switch it off, unplug it, and let it cool completely. Pull the plug, not the cable.
2. Remove the laundry, clean the lint filter, and empty the water tank if fitted.
3. Disconnect any drain or vent hose, then secure the hoses and power cable so they cannot drag or catch.
4. Clear and protect the route. Use two people and a suitable appliance trolley; keep the dryer upright and never lift it by the door or control panel. Protect the cabinet and secure it for transport.
5. At the new location, place it on a firm, level floor and reconnect it according to the installation instructions. Keep ventilation clear and use a suitable socket—no extension lead.
6. The safety policy says to leave it disconnected for **38 hours after moving**. Before reconnecting, check the cable, plug, casing and connections for damage. If anything looks unsafe, leave it unplugged and contact Halvard Home.

Check that the extractor’s wall switch or fused spur is on. Try the light and fan controls to see whether the whole hood has lost power or just the display.

If needed, switch the hood off at its electrical supply for 60 seconds, then switch it back on and try again. Keep your hands dry when operating switches.

If the fan and light work but the screen is still blank, contact Halvard Home support and tell them which controls respond. If nothing works, check whether other kitchen appliances have power. Don’t remove covers or touch internal wiring; arrange a qualified inspection if the problem continues.
Leave the extractor running for 10 minutes after cooking to clear lingering steam and smells.

For a Keel washing machine, finish any wash programme, empty the drum and leave the machine switched on and connected to Wi-Fi. In the Halvard Home app, select the machine and go to **Settings > Firmware update**. Tap **Install** if an update is available, then follow the instructions. Keep the machine powered on and don’t start a wash until the app confirms the update is complete.
Hire a suitably qualified heat pump installer to disconnect, move and recommission the unit. They should handle the fixed electrical and pipework connections; don’t try to relocate it yourself.

To safely relocate your built-in Corra cooktop:

1. **Switch it off and let the glass cool completely.** Remove cookware and loose items.
2. **Isolate the electricity supply.** If it is hardwired, have a qualified electrician disconnect it. Don’t cut, pull, or alter the cable, and don’t assume a dark display means it is isolated.
3. **Have the installer release any fixings or seals.** Don’t pull the cooktop out while it is still secured to the worktop.
4. **Lift it with suitable assistance.** Use two people or lifting equipment, support the parts identified for handling, and don’t lift by the cable, controls, or exposed glass edges. Do not tilt it more than **54 degrees**.
5. **Protect it for transport.** Cushion the glass and casing, secure it against sliding or impact, and don’t put anything on top.
6. **Have it inspected and professionally installed at the new location.** The installer should check stability, ventilation, cable routing, and electrical safety. After moving it, wait **17 hours** before switching it on. If it was dropped, struck, exposed to water, or carried beyond the stated tilt limit, leave it disconnected and have it checked before use.
Yes—if you mean the Lumen smart thermostat, a factory reset erases its saved Wi‑Fi details, heating schedules, and personal settings. Note anything you want to restore before resetting.

Send Halvard Home support your hob’s full model details, a clear photo of the part if you still have it, and a short description of what you need. If the part is missing, describe its purpose instead. Ask them to confirm it’s compatible with your exact model, along with the price, delivery charge and expected delivery time.

Make sure your Mira vacuum is online in the Halvard Home app and that you can start a cleaning from the app. Then open your voice assistant’s app, find the option to add smart-home devices, and search for **Halvard Home**. Sign in with the same Halvard Home account you used to set up Mira, allow access, and ask the assistant to discover devices. Give Mira a simple name, such as “Mira,” then try saying, “Start Mira.”

If it doesn’t appear, check its internet connection, unlink Halvard Home in the assistant app, and link it again.

Make sure the controller is switched on and your phone is connected to your home Wi‑Fi. Turn on Bluetooth, move close to the controller, and allow the companion app any requested Bluetooth, nearby-device or local-network permissions. Then fully close and reopen the app and try adding the controller again. If it still doesn’t appear, restart your phone and check for app updates before contacting the manufacturer’s support.

If you mean the Brio kettle, its warranty lasts **47 months from the delivery date**. Replacement parts fitted during an authorised warranty repair have separate cover for **138 days**. A paid repair has its own **122-day guarantee**.

If you’re leaving food inside, keep the fridge freezer running. Set the fridge to 4°C and the freezer to −18°C, make sure both doors close fully, and remove anything that may expire before you return.

If you’re emptying it for the whole absence, switch it off and unplug it before cleaning. Remove all food, let any ice thaw, wash the interior with warm water and mild detergent, and dry it thoroughly. Leave both doors ajar to help prevent mould and odours. When you return, let it reach its set temperatures before putting chilled or frozen food back in.

Warm, moist air from cooking can condense on the hood’s cold surfaces, especially in winter or when the extraction duct passes through an unheated space. To reduce this, run the hood while cooking and for 10 minutes afterwards, use pan lids where practical, and keep ventilation openings clear. If you see frost, don’t chip it off or apply heat; ask a qualified installer to check the duct insulation and outside vent.

To prepare your Keel washer for a safe move:

1. Switch it off at the socket and unplug it with dry hands. Turn off the water supply and disconnect the hoses as instructed.
2. Drain any remaining water into a tray or onto towels, following the user manual. Empty the drum and leave it dry.
3. Refit the original transport bolts as directed in the manual. They protect the drum during transport. If they’re missing or you can’t fit them safely, contact Halvard Home before moving it.
4. Secure the hoses, cable and door so they can’t swing loose or get trapped.
5. Keep the machine upright where possible, use two people or suitable lifting equipment, and don’t carry it alone. Plan a clear route and don’t lift it by the door, drawer, controls, hoses or cable.

At the new home, remove the transport bolts before using the washer. Follow the installation instructions; the safety policy also says to leave the machine upright and unplugged for 44 hours after moving it before switching it on.

Stop the programme and note the exact code or message. Switch the washer off, unplug it for five minutes, then reconnect it, using dry hands. Check that the door is fully closed and no clothing is caught in the seal; don’t force the door open if water remains inside.

If the code returns, stop using the washer and contact Halvard Home support. Tell them the code and when it appeared.

Warm, moist air may be getting into the fridge freezer. Frequent door opening, uncovered food, or a door that doesn’t seal or close properly can cause frost and dampness.

Cover food, check that nothing blocks the doors or air vents, and clean and dry the door seals. Set the fridge to 4°C. If thick ice keeps returning, contact Halvard Home support.

Provide the cooker hood’s full model details from its rating label and the name or a description of the accessory you need. If you’re unsure what it’s called, send a clear photo of the existing part. Ask support to confirm compatibility, availability, total price including delivery, and expected delivery time before ordering.

Switch on the Mira’s child lock by holding the power button for 3 seconds while the vacuum is on and stationary. A sound confirms it’s active. To unlock it, hold the power button for 3 seconds again and wait for the confirmation sound.

The lock disables the vacuum’s physical buttons, but it does **not** disable scheduled cleaning or controls in the Halvard Home app, so the vacuum may still start automatically. Keep your toddler away while it’s moving.

For the Mira robot vacuum, place it on its plugged-in charging dock. Press and hold the **Power** and **Home** buttons together for 10 seconds, then release them when you hear the reset announcement. Leave it on the dock while it restarts.

The reset erases saved Wi‑Fi details, maps, and cleaning schedules. When the restart is complete, add the vacuum again in the Halvard Home app, reconnect it to Wi‑Fi, and set up new maps or schedules.

If you mean an old **Orrin heat pump**, arrange for a qualified heat pump installer to disconnect it and safely recover its refrigerant—don’t cut pipes, open the refrigerant circuit or dismantle it yourself. Ask your replacement installer about removal and recycling, or contact your council for a service that accepts heat pumps. Check collection arrangements before moving it, keep it upright and away from children while awaiting collection, and use a licensed waste carrier if arranging transport yourself.

Check the dryer’s power supply first: make sure the plug is fully inserted and the wall socket is switched on. You can test the socket with a working lamp. If the socket works, unplug the dryer briefly, reconnect it, close the door firmly, and try again.
Your Vale fridge freezer needs a **2.4 GHz Wi‑Fi network**.

For a cozy home with lower electricity use:

- Set your heating to about **19°C**, then adjust to a comfortable temperature. Lowering it by 1°C may reduce energy use, as long as everyone stays warm enough.
- Use a heating schedule that fits your routine. For a heat pump, keep temperatures fairly steady and try a small overnight reduction rather than switching it off. If you’re away, use a holiday setting or a lower temperature, and keep the heat pump connected to power in cold weather.
- Avoid turning the thermostat sharply higher to warm rooms faster; it generally won’t make them heat faster. Keep furniture and curtains clear of the thermostat.
- On the hob, use the lowest setting that cooks your food, turn it down to a simmer once water boils, and use a lid where possible.
- Set your fridge to **4°C** and freezer to **−18°C**; keep doors closed and avoid blocking air vents.

Don’t change hot-water hygiene settings just to save energy, and follow your installer’s advice if you’re unsure what temperature is suitable for your home.

For a Halvard Home Mira robot vacuum, switch it off and remove it from the charging dock. Check the lid’s edges, hinges and catch for dust, hair or small objects, and wipe accessible edges with a dry, soft cloth. Make sure the dust bin is seated correctly and nothing sticks up above it. Lower the lid gently—don’t force it. If it still won’t close or the hinge or catch looks damaged, stop using the vacuum and contact Halvard Home support.
First, check the cooker hood’s power supply: make sure its wall switch or fused connection switch is on, and check that any plug is fully inserted if you can reach it safely.

Contact Halvard Home customer support with your Keel washer’s model details and a description of the part. Send a clear photo of the identification label, and, if possible, a photo of the existing part. Tell them it’s an additional item, then ask them to confirm it fits your exact model, its availability, the total price including delivery, and the expected delivery time before ordering.

Unplug the kettle and let it cool completely before checking inside. Use a descaler labelled as suitable for kettles, following the package instructions for the amount, water temperature and treatment time. Don’t overfill the kettle or mix cleaning products.

Afterward, empty and rinse it thoroughly. Then fill it to the maximum mark, boil the water and discard it; repeat once before making a drink. Keep the base, plug and outside dry, and never immerse the kettle in water.

First check for anything stopping the door from closing: move food and packaging away from shelf edges, push drawers fully in, and make sure shelves are seated correctly. Clean the door seal and the surface it touches with a soft cloth and warm water, then dry them. Check for freezer ice build-up, but don’t chip it with a sharp tool or force the door shut.

If this is the first installation, check whether the transit spacer is still beneath the freezer door and remove it by hand with the appliance unplugged. If the door still hangs unevenly or the seal is damaged, contact Halvard Home support.

Switch off and unplug the kettle, then let it cool completely. Lift it off the base and dry its outside; check whether water ran down from the spout or lid, and make sure it wasn’t filled above the MAX mark. If water keeps collecting underneath, stop using it and contact Halvard Home support. Don’t immerse the base or try to repair it. If the plug or socket is wet, don’t touch it—switch off power at the consumer unit first.

First, check that the controller’s power supply is on—turn on its clearly labelled wall switch if it has one. If it’s already on, switch it off, wait 30 seconds, then switch it back on. Don’t remove the cover or touch any wiring.

For your Tessa dishwasher, connect it to your home Wi‑Fi, make sure no wash programme is running, empty it and leave it switched on. On the control panel, go to **Settings > Firmware update > Check for updates**. If an update is available, select **Install** and follow the on-screen instructions. Keep the power and Wi‑Fi connected until the display confirms the update is complete.

Pause the programme and wait for the drum to stop. If the door unlocks, spread heavy items evenly around the drum, then restart the programme—don’t force the door open.

Check that the machine is on a hard, level floor, all four feet touch the floor, and it doesn’t rock when gently pushed. If it was newly installed, check the installation guide to confirm the transit bolts were removed. Stop using it and contact Halvard Home support if strong vibration continues.

Stop the cycle and turn off the water supply tap. Switch off and unplug the machine only if the plug and surrounding area are dry—never touch a wet plug or socket. Once it’s safe, wipe up the water and check visible inlet-hose connections, whether the drain hose has slipped out, and whether excess detergent has caused water to run from the drawer.

Don’t run another cycle while the leak is unexplained. If the hoses seem secure or water is coming from beneath the casing, contact Halvard Home support. Do not move the machine or attempt internal repairs.

Before first use:

1. Read the supplied installation instructions and check the required clearances. If they are missing or unclear, contact Halvard Home before installing.
2. Check the dryer for damage. If the casing, door, plug or electrical parts appear damaged, keep it disconnected and report the problem.
3. Choose a dry, ventilated indoor location, away from water, combustible materials and open flames. Keep ventilation openings clear and follow the specified space requirements.
4. Place the dryer on a firm, level floor and adjust its feet so it stands securely without rocking. Don’t improvise supports.
5. Connect any vent hose or drainage as the instructions require, without crushing or twisting it.
6. Plug it directly into a suitable earthed wall socket—never use an extension lead or adaptor. Keep the socket accessible and the lead free from strain, trapping and sharp edges. If the supply or socket is unsuitable, seek qualified help.
7. Remove all packaging from inside and around the drum, then wipe the empty drum with a soft, damp cloth.

Do not connect the dryer if its power lead is damaged or you are unsure about the electrical supply; seek qualified help.

Stop cleaning and switch off the vacuum. If the charging dock or plug is wet, switch off the mains socket before handling it.

Remove the water tank and empty it over a sink. Check that the filler cap is fully closed and inspect the tank and outlet for cracks. Wipe the tank and vacuum’s underside with a dry cloth. Don’t rinse the vacuum body or return it to the dock while it’s wet.

If the tank is cracked, or water leaks again after you refit it securely, stop using the mopping function and contact Halvard Home support.

Make sure the heat pump is switched on and your phone is connected to your home Wi‑Fi. Then try these steps in order:

1. Move your phone closer to the heat pump.
2. Allow the app any requested Bluetooth or local network access in your phone settings.
3. Turn Wi‑Fi off for 10 seconds, then turn it back on.
4. Close and reopen the app, then try adding the heat pump again.
5. Check the app store for an update.

If it still doesn’t appear, contact Halvard Home support and tell them your phone model and what happens when you try to connect.

Check that the washing machine is switched on and your phone is nearby. Connect your phone to a **2.4 GHz Wi‑Fi network**—5 GHz won’t work for setup—and turn on Bluetooth. Allow the app to access nearby devices when prompted.

Close and reopen the Halvard Home app, then try adding the machine again and follow its pairing instructions. If it still doesn’t appear, restart your phone and router and retry once Wi‑Fi is available. If the problem continues, contact Halvard Home support and tell them your phone model and where setup stops.

Yes. During defrosting, ice on the outdoor coil melts and drains beneath the unit, so a puddle can be normal. Monitor it to see whether it stops. If water runs continuously or you’re unsure of its source, contact Halvard Home support or a qualified heat pump engineer.
Heat pumps warm a home gradually, and they typically run at lower temperatures than boilers. So radiators may feel cooler than boiler-heated ones; this does not necessarily mean there is a fault.
The Fenwick cooker hood needs a 2.4 GHz home Wi‑Fi network. It cannot connect to a network set to 5 GHz only.
No. The Halvard Home Brio kettle has no timer or delay-start setting; you must switch it on manually when you’re ready to use it.
Yes. A gentle rumbling or hissing sound while your Brio kettle heats is usually normal. A click when it switches off is expected too.

A rattling, thumping or scraping noise may be caused by loose objects in the drum, metal zips or buttons, an uneven load, or the dryer touching nearby furniture. It may also be unsteady on an uneven floor.

Stop the programme, switch off and unplug the dryer, and let the drum cool before checking for loose items. Redistribute bulky laundry, and make sure the dryer stands level and does not touch a wall or cupboard. Don’t reach underneath or remove any panels.

If the noise continues, or you hear loud grinding, stop using the dryer and contact Halvard Home support.

Stop the programme, switch off and unplug the dryer, and let it cool. Clean and securely refit the fluff filter; if your model has a water tank, empty and refit it. Check that no clothing is trapped in the door and close it firmly.

Reconnect the dryer and try the programme again. If the light keeps flashing, stop using the appliance and contact Halvard Home support. Tell them which light is flashing and when it appears.

Switch off and unplug the machine. If it has been used for a hot wash, let the water cool completely. Open the lower-front filter flap, place towels and a shallow tray underneath, then loosen the filter slowly so trapped water can drain.

Remove debris such as lint, coins or hair, rinse the filter, and refit it securely without forcing it. Run a drain or short rinse cycle to check the drainage and look for leaks. If it still drains slowly or leaks, stop using the machine and contact Halvard Home support.

Switch off the dryer at the socket before unplugging it. Use a torch—not a candle—to check the area. If it’s safe to open the door, carefully remove the laundry, which may be hot, and spread it out so heat can escape.

Once the power supply is stable, plug the dryer back in and switch it on. Check the laundry and restart a suitable programme if it needs more drying. If you notice a burning smell or visible damage, leave the dryer unplugged and contact Halvard Home support.

Make sure the dishwasher is switched on and your phone is connected to your home Wi‑Fi. Then:

1. Move your phone close to the dishwasher.
2. Turn on Bluetooth and allow any nearby-device or location permissions the app requests.
3. Avoid a guest Wi‑Fi network.
4. Close the app completely, reopen it, and try adding the dishwasher again.
5. If it still doesn’t appear, switch the dishwasher off at the mains for 30 seconds, then turn it back on.

If the problem continues, contact Halvard Home support and tell them which steps you’ve tried.

Water underneath your Vale fridge freezer may be from a spill, a blocked defrost drain, or a door that isn’t closing properly. Check for packaging blocking the door and wipe the seals clean. If you can see the drain hole, gently clear loose debris around it—don’t use sharp objects or remove panels.

Switch off and unplug the appliance first, but only if the plug and area are dry; if they’re wet, isolate the power at the fuse box. If the leak returns after restarting, contact Halvard Home support.

A rattling or banging noise can be caused by loose objects in the drum, an uneven load, or a machine that is not level. Pause the programme and wait for the drum to stop and the door to unlock—never force it open. Spread heavy items evenly around the drum, check for coins, keys or other objects, and gently check whether the machine rocks. If it does, switch it off and unplug it before adjusting its feet. If it was newly installed, check the installation guide to make sure the transit bolts have been removed.

To factory reset your Orrin heat pump:

1. Make sure it is switched on and showing no warning.
2. On the controller, open **Settings**.
3. Select **System**, then **Factory reset**.
4. Choose **Confirm** and leave the power connected while the controller restarts.

A factory reset removes saved heating schedules and temperature preferences, so note them down first. When the home screen returns, check the date and time, then set your preferred temperatures and schedule again. If **Factory reset** is unavailable or the controller does not restart, contact Halvard Home support.
Recycle your old Halvard Home Corra induction hob as electrical equipment. Do not put it in your household rubbish bin.

To switch on the Brio kettle’s child lock, make sure it isn’t heating, then press and hold the lock button for three seconds. The lock indicator will light up.

To switch it off, press and hold the same button for three seconds, until the indicator goes out. The lock prevents the kettle from starting a heating cycle; it does not lock the lid or make hot water safe to handle. Keep the kettle and cable out of children’s reach and supervise children.

Connect the fridge freezer to your home Wi-Fi and make sure it has a steady power supply. On the control panel, open **Settings**, select **Software update**, then choose **Check for updates**. If an update is available, follow the on-screen instructions.

Keep the appliance switched on and don’t unplug or restart it during installation. Keep the doors closed as much as possible, and wait for the control panel to confirm the update is complete. If it fails, check your Wi-Fi connection before trying again.

First make sure the kettle has finished boiling and cooled down. Then:

1. Place it securely on its base.
2. Plug in the base and switch on the wall socket.
3. Press and hold the power button for 10 seconds.
4. Release it when the indicator light flashes twice. That confirms the reset is complete.

If the light doesn’t flash, check that the kettle is seated correctly and repeat the steps.

If the machine is damp from condensation, wipe the outside with a soft, dry cloth and improve ventilation. Check nearby hoses and connections; recurring puddles may mean there’s a leak.

If you notice frost, stop using the machine. Switch it off and unplug it only if your hands, plug and socket are dry. Let the machine and room warm naturally—don’t use boiling water, a hairdryer or a portable heater. Once it has thawed, check for visible leaks. If frost returns or you find damaged hoses, contact Halvard Home support before using it again.

Unplug the kettle and let it cool completely. Empty it, open the lid, and gently remove the filter from behind the spout—don’t force it if it’s stuck. Rinse it under warm running water and use a soft brush to loosen limescale. For stubborn deposits, soak the filter in warm water for 10 minutes, then brush gently and rinse thoroughly. Refit it securely before using the kettle.

Avoid abrasive cleaners and metal brushes, and never immerse the kettle body, base, or plug in water.

To factory-reset your Corra induction hob:

1. Remove all cookware and let the cooking zones cool. Make sure the control panel is clean and dry.
2. Switch the hob off with the power button, but leave its electrical supply connected.
3. Press and hold the **timer** and **minus** buttons together for five seconds.
